source.title: Abelian varieties isogenous to no Jacobian
readSections: The published version, freely available from the Annals site (PDF SHA-256 8b76bfac88374180701992e242d88f5d38fbe0b0cdb39c6c40c3c3fbbb874b60, fetched 2026-09-29; no arXiv version exists): all 40 pages, §§1–5 with every proof and the references, read in full by Claude Code session cc-fb70e5; formulas checked on page images where the text layer was ambiguous (pp. 653, 656, 661, 666, 669).

summary: Masser–Zannier prove the main algebraic hypersurface-avoidance theorem for A_g, g≥2: a Hodge-generic principally polarized abelian variety over a field of degree at most 2^{16g⁴} is isogenous to nothing in a given algebraic hypersurface. Their quantitative counting and density results imply examples isogenous to no Jacobian for g≥4, and they also prove a genus-one analogue. The proof combines isogeny and endomorphism estimates, Pila blocks, functional transcendence, Galois genericity, and theta-model degree bounds. The current inventory has 74 items (3 library,11 planned,60 missing), nine routes, nineteen prerequisites and fourteen source diagnostics. The quantitative isogeny and CM-orbit suppliers remain shared Part II imports; early counting stays at LD.6 while definable uniformization, weakly-special geometry and Ax–Lindemann belong to the accepted LogicAndDefinabilityPartII. The dedicated AbelianVarietiesIsogenousToNoJacobian roadmap owns the paper-specific arithmetic applications. Verified fixes isolate the unsupported supplementary rational 16-torsion assertion as gated item /73, reject the global closed transcendental analytic hypersurface by /74, and retain the compact real-analytic interpolation image in /66. A local replacement and the full arithmetic torsion descent/degree comparison remain explicitly unresolved; neither affects the main Theorem 1.1 statement.

items.name: Siegel moduli space A_g and its finite covers
items.statement: A_g is the (coarse) moduli space of principally polarized abelian varieties of dimension g, of dimension G = g(g+1)/2, defined over Q. A finite cover Ã → A_g is a variety with a generically finite dominant map to A_g, both over Q̄; the paper uses rational maps Ψ : Ã → A^G that are finite (generically finite-to-one) with degree D_Ψ and field of definition F_Ψ.
items.note: PELModuli owns the Siegel moduli problem; the covers used are the level Γ(16, 32) theta covers of §5.2 (item on V_e).

items.name: Isogeny of abelian varieties, not respecting polarizations
items.statement: An isogeny A → B of abelian varieties over a field is a surjective homomorphism with finite kernel; isogenies and isomorphisms in the paper are not required to respect polarizations. A and B are isogenous if an isogeny exists.
items.note: Tau Ceti's IsIsogeny: finite surjective homomorphism of abelian varieties over a field.

items.name: Jacobian locus in A_g and its closure
items.statement: The Jacobian (Torelli) locus of A_g is the image of the moduli of smooth curves of genus g under C ↦ (Jac C, θ); its closure consists of Jacobians of stable curves of compact type. It has dimension 3g − 3, so for g ≥ 4 (where 3g − 3 < G) it lies in an algebraic hypersurface H of A_g; for g ≤ 3 every principally polarized abelian variety is isomorphic to the Jacobian of a stable curve, and every abelian variety is isogenous to a principally polarized one.
items.note: The Tau Ceti JacobianChallenge builds the Jacobian of one curve over a field; the Torelli map to A_g and its closure are not planned.

items.name: Hodge generic principally polarized abelian variety
items.statement: A in A_g(C) is Hodge generic if the Mumford–Tate group of the rational Hodge structure H¹(A, Q) is GSp_{2g}. A Hodge generic A is simple with End(A) = Z. An elliptic curve is Hodge generic if and only if it has no complex multiplication.
items.note: Review: the equivalence with lying in no proper special subvariety of A_g, and the countable-union statement, need A_g, which is downstream of ShimuraData D1 and D4; they moved to item 22, in route 1. No layer of the atlas mentions Mumford–Tate groups.

items.name: Galois generic and p-Galois generic abelian varieties
items.statement: An abelian variety A of dimension g over a number field k is p-Galois generic if the image of Gal(k̄/k) acting on the p-power torsion A[p^∞] is open in GSp_{2g}(Z_p), and Galois generic if the image in GSp_{2g}(Ẑ) (on all torsion) is open.

items.name: p-Galois generic implies Galois generic implies Hodge generic
items.statement: If A over a number field is p-Galois generic for one prime p, then it is Galois generic (Cadoret [5, Th. 1.2]); a Galois generic A is Hodge generic (Pink [36, p. 274]). Being p-Galois generic is invariant under isogeny and Galois conjugation.
items.note: Review: moved from ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations R01.6 to route 7. Serre's open-image theorem rests on Faltings' semisimplicity and isogeny theorem (FaltingsFinitenessAndIsogenyTheorems R28.4), and R01.6 → R28.4 is an edge of the atlas; Deligne's lemma needs A_g (PELModuli M2, M5), which is not upstream of R01.6; Pink's implication uses Deligne's theorem that Hodge classes on abelian varieties are absolutely Hodge, which no layer plans.

items.name: Abelian varieties with complex multiplication
items.statement: A (principally polarized) abelian variety has complex multiplication (CM) if its endomorphism algebra contains a commutative semisimple subalgebra of degree 2g; CM points are the special points of A_g.

items.name: Siegel upper half-space and the action of Sp_2g
items.statement: H_g is the space of complex symmetric g × g matrices τ = x + iy with y > 0; Sp_{2g}(R) acts by τ ↦ (aτ + b)(cτ + d)^{-1}, and A_g(C) = Sp_{2g}(Z)\H_g with J : H_g → A_g the uniformisation.
items.note: ShimuraData D5 constructs all Siegel data, with X = H_g^± and its compact dual. AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A5 plans the Riemann bilinear relations, polarized complex tori and the Siegel universal analytic family with its monodromy, which give A_g(C) = Sp_2g(Z)\H_g and the uniformisation J (review).

items.name: Estimates on the Siegel fundamental domain
items.statement: Siegel's fundamental domain F_g ⊂ H_g ([18, p. 194]) is the set of τ = x + iy with y Minkowski-reduced, |x_ij| ≤ 1/2 for all i, j, and |det(cτ + d)| ≥ 1 for every (a b; c d) ∈ Sp_2g(Z); every point of H_g is Sp_2g(Z)-equivalent to a point of F_g, and F_g is semialgebraic, hence definable. There is δ = δ(g) ∈ (0, 1] such that every τ ∈ F_g satisfies δ^{-1}y^{(0)} ≥ y ≥ δy^{(0)} and y^{(0)} ≥ δι (23), where y^{(0)} is the diagonal matrix with the diagonal entries y_1, …, y_g of y; moreover √3/2 ≤ y_1 ≤ ··· ≤ y_g (24) and |x_ij| ≤ 1/2 ([18, Cor. 2, p. 193; p. 192; Lemma 15, p. 195; (S.3), p. 194]).
items.note: No layer plans Siegel's fundamental domain for Sp_2g(Z), Minkowski reduction or Igusa's estimates. AdelicAlgebraicGroups AA.3 plans general reduction theory (Siegel sets with height estimates, finitely many covering the arithmetic quotient), from which bounds of type (23) on a Siegel set of Sp_2g would also follow (review). MOK-PILA-TSIMERMAN-19's accepted item 38 (Siegel sets and fundamental domains) is planned in AA.3 and ShimuraVarieties V0; what is new here is the classical Minkowski-reduced domain with Igusa's estimates (23)–(24).

items.name: The upper half-plane and the SL₂(Z) fundamental domain
items.statement: The upper half-plane H, the standard fundamental domain F for SL₂(Z) (|x| ≤ 1/2, |τ| ≥ 1), and the fact that every τ has an SL₂(Z)-translate in F; for τ ∈ F, y ≥ √3/2.

items.name: The elliptic modular function j and the j-invariant
items.statement: The j-invariant of an elliptic curve (Weierstrass j = c₄³/Δ) and the elliptic modular function j on H with j(τ) = j(E_τ) for E_τ = C/(Zτ + Z); the model E_j of (6) has invariant j for j ≠ 0, 1728.
items.note: Mathlib has the algebraic j-invariant WeierstrassCurve.j. ModularCurvesPartII R12.1 plans the uniformisation E ≅ C/Λ and the Weierstrass curve of a lattice; Tau Ceti ModularForms layer 0 plans the analytic j = E₄³/Δ with modular invariance and q-expansion. Neither states the identity j(τ) = j(C/(Zτ + Z)) connecting them (review).

items.name: Modular polynomials Φ_m
items.statement: For m ≥ 1 the modular polynomial Φ_m ∈ Z[x, y] is monic in each variable, of degree ψ(m) = m∏_{p|m}(1 + 1/p) ≤ Σ_{d|m} d in each variable and irreducible, and Φ_m(j(E), j(E′)) = 0 if and only if there is a cyclic isogeny of degree m between E and E′. Isogenous elliptic curves admit a cyclic isogeny between them.
items.locator: §3.1 (ii), (v), p. 645; Lemma 3.1 and its proof, pp. 646–647

items.name: Weil height of j and Faltings height of an abelian variety
items.statement: h denotes the absolute logarithmic Weil height of an algebraic number, and h(A) the logarithmic semistable Faltings height of an abelian variety over Q̄ (not always non-negative).
items.note: Mathlib has the absolute logarithmic Weil height of an algebraic number, NumberField.absLogHeight₁, normalised through ℚ⟮x⟯ and so independent of the field; DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence DT.0 plans Weil heights generally. The stable Faltings height is ArakelovGeometryAndAbelianHeights R35.3's, and it is the part still planned (review).

items.name: Faltings height under isogeny
items.statement: If A and Ã are related by an isogeny of degree m̃, then h(Ã) ≤ h(A) + ½ log m̃.

items.name: Rational and complex representations, Rosati length and the discriminant D(A)
items.statement: For A principally polarized with period matrix τ = x + iy, an endomorphism v gives κ(v) ∈ M_g(C) and ρ(v) ∈ M_2g(Z) with κ(ι τ) = (ι τ)ρ (21). The Rosati form gives the length ℓ(v)² = tr(ρερ^tε^{-1}) = 2 tr(κ y κ̄^t y^{-1}) (22, corrected, see E1), with ε the standard symplectic matrix; ℓ(v) ≥ 1 for v ≠ 0 and ℓ(n) = √(2g) n. D(A) = det(tr(ρ_i ερ_j^t ε^{-1})) over a Z-basis of End(A) is the discriminant of End(A) for the Rosati form.
items.note: The Rosati involution itself is planned in AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A2; the analytic length and discriminant are not. The D(A) display on p. 655 repeats the slip of E1 and is recorded as E9; the statement here uses the rational Rosati trace form, as [27] does.

items.name: Definable sets and the algebraic part
items.statement: Sets definable in an o-minimal expansion of the real field (here R_an,exp); for a definable W, the algebraic part W^alg is the union of all connected positive-dimensional semialgebraic subsets of W.

items.name: Pila–Wilkie counting theorem
items.statement: For W definable and ε > 0, the number of rational points of W − W^alg of height at most T is ≪_{W,ε} T^ε.

items.name: Pila's blocks: uniform counting of integral points in definable families
items.statement: Blocks and basic blocks as in Pila [32, Def. 3.1–3.2]. For a definable family (W_τ) and ε > 0, the integral points of W_τ with coordinates bounded by T lie in ≪_ε T^ε basic blocks, uniformly in the parameter τ ([32, Th. 3.5(2)]); a block of positive dimension lies in W^alg ([32, Prop. 3.4(2)]); and the image of a block under a semialgebraic map is a block ([32, Def. 3.2(2)]).

items.name: Definability of the uniformisation on fundamental domains
items.statement: The restriction of j to the fundamental domain F, and of J : H_g → A_g to the Siegel fundamental domain F_g, are definable in R_an,exp (Peterzil–Starchenko [31]; F is definable though not compact, [46, Ch. 4, Notes]).

items.name: No algebraic arcs over non-modular curves (Ax–Lindemann for j²)
items.statement: If C_C ⊂ C² is an absolutely irreducible algebraic curve that is not modular (not a vertical or horizontal line and not given by some Φ_m), then Z = F² ∩ (j²)^{-1}(C_C) contains no real algebraic arc, so Z^alg = ∅ (Pila [33, Th. 1.6]; [46, Lemma 4.4]).

The curve is then modular or vertical/horizontal, contradicting the stated exclusions. These exclusions cannot be dropped; retain the original paper-specific deduction rather than rebuilding functional transcendence.

items.name: Ax–Lindemann for A_g (Pila–Tsimerman)
items.statement: If Γ is a semialgebraic curve contained in J^{-1}(H) for an algebraic subvariety H of A_g, then there is a weakly special subvariety K ⊂ H with Γ ⊂ J^{-1}(K) (Pila–Tsimerman [34, Th. 6.1]).

proofOutline: Use the shared Ax–Lindemann deduction from functional transcendence in LogicAndDefinabilityPartII, with the Siegel uniformization and its algebraic domain structure explicitly identified.

A positive-dimensional semialgebraic lift of an algebraic subvariety yields a weakly special subvariety containing the lift image and contained in that subvariety. The arithmetic application combines this with /23 and its proper-hypersurface and Hodge-generic hypotheses.

items.name: Weakly special subvarieties and their bi-algebraic characterisation
items.statement: Weakly special subvarieties of A_g (in the sense of Pink and Ullmo–Yafaev); by Ullmo–Yafaev [45, Th. 1.2] they are exactly the bi-algebraic subvarieties (algebraic subvarieties whose preimage in H_g has algebraic components). A point of A_g(C) is Hodge generic (item 4) if and only if it lies in no proper special subvariety, and the points that are not Hodge generic lie in a countable union of proper special subvarieties (§1.2, p. 637).

tests: Every point is weakly special; a Hodge-generic point may therefore lie in a proper weakly special zero-dimensional subvariety.
Vertical and horizontal curves and modular correspondences in the j² case are allowed weakly special cases.

items.name: Weakly special subvarieties through a Hodge generic point
items.statement: A weakly special subvariety of A_g that contains a Hodge generic point is either a point or all of A_g (Gao, appendix to André–Corvaja–Zannier [2], Lemma 10.2.6 (ii) ⇒ (iv), with Ullmo–Yafaev).

Only a positive-dimensional weakly special K inside a proper hypersurface contradicts Hodge genericity.

items.name: Serre's open image for End = Z in dimensions g odd, 2 and 6
items.statement: If g is odd or g ∈ {2, 6} and A over a number field has End(A) = Z, then A is p-Galois generic for every p (Serre [39, p. 35]). For g = 4, End(A) = Z does not suffice.
items.note: Review: moved from ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations R01.6 to route 7. Serre's open-image theorem rests on Faltings' semisimplicity and isogeny theorem (FaltingsFinitenessAndIsogenyTheorems R28.4), and R01.6 → R28.4 is an edge of the atlas; Deligne's lemma needs A_g (PELModuli M2, M5), which is not upstream of R01.6; Pink's implication uses Deligne's theorem that Hodge classes on abelian varieties are absolutely Hodge, which no layer plans.

items.name: Open monodromy of the universal family over A_g
items.statement: For generic x of A^G and A_x in the projection of Ψ^{-1}(x), defined over a finite extension k_x of Q(x), the Galois group of k_x(A_x[p^∞])/k_x contains an open subgroup of Sp_{2g}(Z_p) (Deligne, Hodge II, Lemma 4.4.16), and is therefore open in GSp_{2g}(Z_p) by the Weil pairing.
items.note: AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A5 plans the Siegel universal analytic family and its monodromy, the topological input to Deligne's lemma; LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles LPV.5 plans open symplectic monodromy only for Lefschetz pencils. The arithmetic statement over the function field is planned nowhere (review). Review: moved from ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations R01.6 to route 7. Serre's open-image theorem rests on Faltings' semisimplicity and isogeny theorem (FaltingsFinitenessAndIsogenyTheorems R28.4), and R01.6 → R28.4 is an edge of the atlas; Deligne's lemma needs A_g (PELModuli M2, M5), which is not upstream of R01.6; Pink's implication uses Deligne's theorem that Hodge classes on abelian varieties are absolutely Hodge, which no layer plans.

items.name: Specialisation of endomorphism rings (Masser)
items.statement: For a family whose generic endomorphism ring is Z, the number of integral n ∈ [1, N]^G whose fibre has End ≠ Z is ≪ N^{G−1}(log N)^µ with µ = µ(g) (Masser [23, main theorem]).

items.name: Hilbert irreducibility with Frattini and Cohen's count
items.statement: Let G be a profinite group whose Frattini subgroup N, the intersection of its maximal open subgroups, is open; a closed subgroup H with H·N = G equals G. If G is an open subgroup of GSp_2g(Z_p), then N is open (Serre [38, Prop. (iv), p. 148; Example 1, p. 149]). For a finite Galois cover with group G/N of a variety over a number field k, there is a thin set Ω ⊂ k^G outside which the decomposition group of the specialisation is the whole group (Serre [38, Prop. 2, p. 123], with the assumption 'Ram' of p. 149), and Ω ∩ Q^G is thin in Q^G ([38, Prop., p. 128]). A thin subset of Q^G contains ≪ N^{G−1/2} log N integral points n with 1 ≤ n_i ≤ N (Cohen [9, p. 229]; [38, p. 177]), and the exponent 1/2 cannot be improved in general.
items.note: Hilbert irreducibility for regular finite Galois covers over number fields is planned in InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups IG.2. Tau Ceti ProfiniteProPGroups layer 3 plans the profinite Frattini subgroup and its non-generation property for pro-p groups only. The openness of the Frattini subgroup of an open subgroup of GSp_2g(Z_p), thin sets and Cohen's count are planned nowhere (review).

items.name: Minkowski's second theorem for the endomorphism lattice
items.statement: End(A × Ã) of rank r contains linearly independent v_1, …, v_r with ℓ(v_1)···ℓ(v_r) ≪_g D(A × Ã)^{1/2} (Geometry of Numbers, successive minima).
items.note: Mathlib has Minkowski's first (convex body) theorem; the second (successive minima) is GN.1's.

items.name: Frattini subgroup
items.statement: The Frattini subgroup Φ(G) of a group G is the intersection of its maximal subgroups; when the lattice of subgroups of G is coatomic (for instance G finite), a subgroup H with H ⊔ Φ(G) = G equals G.
items.note: Mathlib's frattini is the abstract Frattini subgroup, which for a profinite group need not be the intersection of the maximal open subgroups. The profinite form used in the proof of Lemma 5.1 (p. 659), with the openness of the Frattini subgroup of an open subgroup of GSp_2g(Z_p), is part of item 27; Tau Ceti ProfiniteProPGroups layer 3 plans it for pro-p groups (review).

items.name: Lemma 2.1: integer matrices of elliptic isogenies
items.statement: If E, Ẽ are related by an isogeny of degree m and τ, τ̃ ∈ F satisfy j(τ) = j(E), j(τ̃) = j(Ẽ), then τ̃ = (aτ + b)/(cτ + d) with a, b, c, d ∈ Z, ad − bc = m and max{|a|, |b|, |c|, |d|} ≤ 2m^{3/2}.
items.note: The classical input, that an isogeny of degree m from C/(Zτ̃ + Z) to C/(Zτ + Z) is multiplication by some κ with [Zτ + Z : κ(Zτ̃ + Z)] = m, so that τ̃ = (aτ + b)/(cτ + d) with ad − bc = m, is the g = 1 case of the representations of item 15 and rests on the uniformisation by C/Λ that ModularCurvesPartII R12.1 plans (review).

items.name: Lemma 2.2: isogeny estimate for elliptic curves
items.statement: If E, Ẽ are isogenous elliptic curves defined over a number field of degree at most D ≥ 2, there is an isogeny between them of degree at most c D²(log D)²(1 + h(j(E)))² with c absolute (Masser–Wüstholz [24] with exponent 4 on the height; Gaudron–Rémond [15] as stated, with explicit c).

items.name: Counting finite subgroups of given order
items.statement: The number of subgroups of (Q/Z)^{2g} of order at most m is ≪_g m^{2g}, and at most m² when g = 1 (Lemma 6.1 of [26, p. 469], as used at the end of §2 and in the proof of Lemma 5.1(b)).
items.locator: End of §2, p. 644; proof of Lemma 5.1 (b), p. 658

items.name: Many isogeny classes among E_{n1+in2}
items.statement: The curves E_j, j = n1 + in2 with 1 ≤ n1, n2 ≤ N, represent at least C_0^{-1} N²/(log N)⁴ isogeny classes, C_0 > 0 absolute.

items.name: Lemma 3.1: elimination
items.statement: Given f ≠ 0 in C[y1, y2] there is c = c(f) such that for every m there is G_m ≠ 0 in C[x1, x2] of degree at most cψ(m)² with G_m(ξ1, ξ2) = 0 whenever Φ_m(ξ1, η1) = Φ_m(ξ2, η2) = f(η1, η2) = 0.
items.note: Proved by iterated resultants. Mathlib has Polynomial.resultant (Mathlib/RingTheory/Polynomial/Resultant/Basic.lean), with resultant_eq_zero_iff over a field, which is the tool the proof uses; the lemma itself is missing, and it needs the modular polynomials of item 12 (irreducible, of degree ψ(m) in each variable).

items.name: Lemma 3.2: few candidates with small-degree isogenies
items.statement: Given integers M ≥ 2 and N ≥ 1, there are only ≪_f N M³ log M pairs n = (n1, n2) with 1 ≤ n1, n2 ≤ N such that E_n (j = n1 + in2) is isogenous to its complex conjugate or to some E_c with c ∈ C via an isogeny of degree at most M.

items.name: Lemma 3.3: large field degree from a large isogeny
items.statement: If E_n is isogenous to Ẽ = E_c with c ∈ C and n outside the exceptions of Lemma 3.2 with M = [(log N)³], then there is an isogeny of degree m̃ ≪ D̃⁷, where D̃ ≥ 2 bounds the degree of a field of definition of Ẽ, and log N ≪ D̃²(log D̃)².
items.note: D̃ enters twice: as an upper bound for [K̃ : Q] here, and on p. 650 as a lower bound for the number of distinct conjugates σ(c) of c over Q(i) and the coefficients of f. So take D̃ = max{2, [K̃ : Q]} with K̃ = Q(c), the field of definition of E_c in the model (6).

items.name: Theorem 1.7: elliptic curves not isogenous to a real algebraic curve
items.statement: Given a real algebraic curve C in A_1(C) = R², there is C = C(C) such that for every integer N ≥ 2 there are at most C N(log N)^{10} pairs of integers 1 ≤ n1, n2 ≤ N for which E_j, j = n1 + in2, either has complex multiplication or is isogenous to some E_c with c ∈ C.

items.name: André's theorem on CM pairs
items.statement: André [1]: an irreducible algebraic curve in C² containing infinitely many points (j1, j2) whose coordinates are both singular moduli (CM j-invariants) is special, that is, a component of some Φ_N(X, Y) = 0 or a line X = j0 or Y = j0 with j0 singular. Effective versions are due to Kühne [21] and Bilu–Masser–Zannier [4]. The paper uses it only in the remark on p. 648, for curves f = 0 involving both variables, where the exception is f = Φm up to constants.
items.note: LD.6 includes source-scoped André–Oort cases.

items.name: One-parameter families j = n + in0
items.statement: For C given by f of degree at most d ≥ 1 in each variable there is an integer n0 with 0 ≤ n0 ≤ 2d³ + 1 such that Theorem 1.7 holds for j = n + in0 (n = 1, …, N) (sketch).
items.note: Sketched in the paper, which does not state the count for the family j = n + in0. The sketch shows that Gm(x + in0, x − in0) ≡ 0 forces ψ(m) ≤ d, then excludes at most deg Gm ≤ 2dψ(m)² values of n0 for one m. Since every m with ψ(m) ≤ d (hence m ≤ d) must be avoided at once, the argument as written gives some 1 ≤ n0 ≤ 2d⁴ + 1; the printed 2d³ + 1 needs a further argument (E10).

items.name: A real-analytic curve meeting every isogeny class
items.statement: There is a bounded real-analytic curve Z ⊂ C (with |j| ≤ 2079 + e^{4π}) such that every elliptic curve over Q̄ is isogenous to one with j ∈ Z; by Theorem 1.7 it is transcendental. Construction by a Newton interpolation series F(t) = a0 + Σ a_n ∏(t − t_m)/(t_n − t_m).

items.name: Lemma 4.1: entries of the rational representation
items.statement: Given g ≥ 1 and 0 < δ ≤ 1 there is C = C(g, δ) such that if τ = x + iy for A satisfies (23) and |x_ij| ≤ δ^{-1}, then for every endomorphism v with ρ(v) = (a −b; −c d): |a_ij| ≤ C√(y_i/y_j) ℓ(v), |b_ij| ≤ C√(y_i y_j) ℓ(v), |c_ij| ≤ C ℓ(v)/√(y_i y_j), |d_ij| ≤ C√(y_j/y_i) ℓ(v).

items.name: Lemma 4.2: an isogeny of controlled length
items.statement: There is c = c(g) such that for isogenous principally polarized A, Ã of dimension g there are isogenies f : A → Ã and f̃ : Ã → A such that v(α, α̃) = (f̃(α̃), f(α)) on A × Ã has ℓ(v) ≤ c D(A × Ã)^{1/2}; consequently (deg f)(deg f̃) = deg v ≤ ℓ(v)^{4g} (31).

items.name: Lemma 4.3: the imaginary part is bounded by the height
items.statement: Given g ≥ 1 and 0 < δ ≤ 1 there is C = C(g, δ) such that if τ = x + iy for A, defined over a number field of degree at most D, satisfies y ≥ δy^{(0)} and y^{(0)} ≥ δι, then y_i ≤ C D max{1, h(A)} for i = 1, …, g.

items.name: Heights bound cusp forms from below at algebraic points (Masser–Wüstholz)
items.statement: There are cusp forms φ_1, …, φ_r on Sp_{2g}(Z) of equal weight with rational Fourier coefficients and no common zero; for τ corresponding to A over a field of degree ≤ D and u = φ_k(τ) ≠ 0, D^{-1} log max{1, |u|^{-1}} ≪ max{1, h(A)} ([25, Lemmas 8.4 and 8.6], with h(O) ≪ max{1, h(A)} by [25, (7.4)]); and |φ(τ)| ≤ M exp(−2πc tr(y)) under the weakened reduction hypotheses (Igusa [18, Lemma 20]).

items.name: Lemma 4.4: endomorphism estimate (Masser–Wüstholz)
items.statement: There are c = c(g) and λ = λ(g) such that if A is defined over a number field of degree at most D, then D(A) ≤ c max{D, h(A)}^λ (main theorem of [27] with its inequality for C, δ = 1).

items.name: Isogeny estimates for abelian varieties (Masser–Wüstholz)
items.statement: If abelian varieties A, B over a number field of degree D are isogenous, there is an isogeny of degree bounded by a polynomial in D and h(A) with exponents depending on g ([26]); used for the isogeny-class counts of §5.3.
items.locator: §5.3, pp. 666–667 (isogeny-class counts; thinning in the proof of Corollary 1.4); outlined in §1.3, p. 641, where it is cited as [25]

items.name: Lemma 5.1: candidates avoiding small isogenies and Galois degeneracy
items.statement: There is µ = µ(g) such that for integers M ≥ 1 and N ≥ 2 there are only ≪ N^{G−1}M^{2g} + N^{G−1}(log N)^µ + N^{G−1/2} log N elements n ∈ [1, N]^G such that some A_n in the projection of Ψ^{-1}(n) is (a) not defined over an extension of Q of degree at most D (1), (b) isogenous to some Ã in H via an isogeny to Ã of degree at most M, or (c) not p-Galois generic, for a fixed prime p (p = 2 will do); the implied constant depends only on Ã, Ψ, H. For g odd or g = 2, 6 the last term can be omitted.

items.name: Lemma 5.2: isogeny degree and heights
items.statement: If A = A_n as in Lemma 5.1 is isogenous to some Ã in H, there is an isogeny f : A → Ã of degree m̃ ≪ max{D̃, log N}^{2gλ} (33), with D(A × Ã) ≪ max{D̃, log N + h(Ã)}^λ (34) and max{1, h(A), h(Ã)} ≪ log N + log m̃ (35), where D̃ ≥ 2 bounds the degree of a field of definition of Ã. Choosing M = [(log N)^ν] for a fixed ν > 2gλ in Lemma 5.1, any n outside its exceptional set (now ≪ N^{G−γ}(log N)^{2gν} elements) has M < m̃, hence (log N)^ν ≪ m̃ ≪ D̃^{2gλ} (36).

items.name: Integral points on the isogeny correspondence lie in zero-dimensional blocks
items.statement: For τ ∈ H_g let W_τ = {X ∈ M_2(M_g(R)) : det(x_cτ + x_d) ≠ 0, (x_aτ + x_b)(x_cτ + x_d)^{-1} ∈ Z} with Z = F_g ∩ J^{-1}(H). The integral points ρ_σ attached to the Galois conjugates Ã^σ satisfy ‖ρ_σ‖ ≪ D̃^λ (45, assuming λ ≥ 4), and the blocks containing them have zero-dimensional image in Z because a positive-dimensional one would give a weakly special K ⊂ H through the Hodge generic Ã^σ; hence D̃ ≪ 1.
items.note: The count "the number of different π_τ(ρ_σ) = τ̃_σ is ≫ D̃" (p. 663) needs D̃ comparable to the number of Galois conjugates of the moduli point of Ã, so D̃ is taken as the degree of a field of definition of bounded degree over the field of moduli (item 72; compare item 36) (review).

items.name: Λ-forms: Siegel modular forms for a normal subgroup
items.statement: For Λ normal of index n in Γ = Sp_{2g}(Z) and ∆(γ, τ) = det(rτ + s), an analytic ϕ on H_g is a Λ-form of weight k if ϕ(λ(τ)) = ∆(λ, τ)^k ϕ(τ) for λ ∈ Λ. For g ≥ 2 it has a Fourier expansion Σ a(M) exp(πi tr(Mτ)) over positive semidefinite symmetric M with dM half-integral, and ord(ϕ) = min_{a(M) ≠ 0} tr(M), with ord(ϕ1ϕ2) ≥ ord(ϕ1) + ord(ϕ2).
items.note: Partly planned elsewhere (review). AutomorphicBundles B4 plans classical forms for Siegel data, with the analytic transformation law and the cocycle identity, and B5 plans Fourier expansions; ShimuraVarieties V2 records when Koecher's principle may be used. Only the order function ord and its superadditivity are missing; route 7 imports the rest.

items.name: Lemma 5.3: the norm of a Λ-form
items.statement: If ϕ is a Λ-form of weight k and Γ = ∪ γ_iΛ = ∪ Λγ_i (i = 1, …, n, γ_1 = 1), then Φ_1(τ) = ∏_{i≥2} ϕ(γ_i(τ))/∆(γ_i, τ)^k is a Λ-form of weight (n − 1)k and Φ = ϕΦ_1 is a Γ-form of weight nk.

items.name: Igusa's order bound for Siegel modular forms
items.statement: A nonzero Γ-form of weight k has ord ≤ κ_g k/(4π), with κ_g ≤ (2g/√3)c_g for the Minkowski constant c_g ≤ (4/π)^g Γ((g+1)/2)² (3/2)^{(g−1)(g−2)} (Igusa [18, Th. 7 p. 206, p. 197]; Lekkerkerker [22, p. 63]).

items.name: Lemma 5.4: order bound for Λ-forms
items.statement: A nonzero Λ-form ϕ of weight k satisfies ord(ϕ) ≤ κ_g n k/(4π).

items.name: Theta constants of level Γ(e, 2e)
items.statement: θ_{mm*}(τ) = Σ_{h∈Z^g} exp{πi(h + m)τ(h + m)^t + 2πi(h + m)m*^t} for row vectors m, m* ∈ R^g. For an even integer e, Λ = Γ(e, 2e) is normal in Γ = Sp_{2g}(Z), and the θ_{m0}(eτ)² (m ∈ e^{-1}Z^g/Z^g) are Λ-forms of weight 1, whose Fourier expansions may be taken with d = e. The variety V_e parametrised by the θ_{m0}(eτ) is quasi-projective when 8 | e (Igusa [18, p. 415], with e also a square).

items.name: Lemma 5.5: a Siegel lemma for theta polynomials
items.statement: Given C-linear combinations χ_1, …, χ_{G+2} of the θ_{m0}(eτ), a real W ≥ 0 and an integer D ≥ 0 with (D + 1)^{G+1} > (G + 1)!(4eW + 1)^G (48), there is a nonzero homogeneous P ∈ C[X_1, …, X_{G+2}] of degree D such that ϕ = P(χ_1², …, χ_{G+2}²), if nonzero, has ord(ϕ) > W: its coefficients a(M) vanish for every M with eM half-integral and tr(M) ≤ W, of which there are at most (4eW + 1)^G. The paper prints "ord(ϕ) ≥ W", which is too weak for the application with W = Nk; the proof gives the strict form (E11).

items.name: Degree of the level-(16, 32) theta model of A_g
items.statement: The Zariski closure of V_16 has degree at most 2(G + 1)!((32g/(π√3)) 512^{2g²} c_g)^G ≤ 2^{16g⁴−1}; with Ã = V_16 (analytically Γ(16, 32)\H_g) and Ψ given by suitable θ_{m0}(16τ)/θ_{00}(16τ), D_Ψ ≤ 2^{16g⁴−1} and F_Ψ = F̃ = Q. Here n = [Γ : Γ(e, 2e)] ≤ e^{2g²}(2e)^{2g²}.
items.note: This is the theta-coordinate/geometric degree estimate. A Q-model of V_16, its complex congruence quotient, an arithmetic fine-level model with universal principally polarized scheme, and a torsion field are separate objects. The unsupported identification with full rational 16-torsion is E14 and is isolated as gated item /73. Preserve the original numerical bound for the main theorem without attributing torsion to its coordinate field.
tests: At τ=iI_g the theta quotients θ_{m0}(16τ)/θ_{00}(16τ) are positive real. Under the asserted algebraic forgetful map their algebraic coordinate field is real, which cannot be a field of full rational 16-torsion for a principally polarized A.
The projective degree estimate D_Ψ does not itself bound the field needed to split the torsion representation.

items.name: Theorem 1.3: almost all points of bounded degree are isogenous to nothing in H
items.statement: For g ≥ 2, a finite cover Ã of A_g, a finite map Ψ : Ã → A^G, an algebraic hypersurface H ⊂ A_g and γ < 1/2, there are C = C(Ã, Ψ, H, γ) and D = D(Ã, Ψ) = [F̃ : Q][F_Ψ : Q]D_Ψ (1) such that for every N ≥ 1 at most C N^{G−γ} elements n ∈ [1, N]^G have a point of Ψ^{-1}(n) whose projection to A_g is (a) not defined over an extension of Q of degree at most D, or (b) isogenous to some B in H; the remaining ones can be taken Galois (hence Hodge) generic ('strong Theorem 1.3'); for g odd or g = 2, 6 any γ < 1 works; and there are Ã, Ψ over Q with D(Ã, Ψ) = 2^{16g⁴}.
items.note: The degree D=[F̃:Q][F_Ψ:Q]D_Ψ is the main theorem’s bound. Any supplementary arithmetic-level comparison must separately track descent and torsion extensions; /73 cannot reuse this D without a proof.

items.name: Theorem 1.1: a Hodge generic point isogenous to nothing in a hypersurface
items.statement: Given an algebraic hypersurface H in A_g with g ≥ 2, there is A in A_g, defined over an extension of Q of degree at most 2^{16g⁴} and Hodge generic, that is not isogenous to any B in H.
items.note: Theorem 1.1 as printed has no torsion clause. The sentence immediately after it is a supplementary claim, isolated as /73 and gated by E14. The main Hodge-generic hypersurface-avoidance theorem and its field-degree bound are preserved.

items.name: Corollary 1.2: abelian varieties isogenous to no Jacobian
items.statement: For every g ≥ 4 there is a principally polarized abelian variety of dimension g, defined over an extension of Q of degree at most 2^{16g⁴} and Hodge generic, that is not isogenous to any Jacobian.

items.name: Corollary 1.4: a dense set of pairwise non-isogenous examples
items.statement: For every g ≥ 4 there is a set of principally polarized abelian varieties of dimension g, dense in the euclidean topology, each defined over an extension of Q of degree at most 2^{16g⁴} and not isogenous to any of the others or to any Jacobian.

items.name: Theorem 1.5: unirational A_g for g ≤ 5
items.statement: For g = 2, 3, 4, 5, assume a dominant rational map Ξ : A^G → A_g over Q. For every hypersurface H ⊂ A_g and γ < 1/2 there is C = C(Ξ, H, γ) such that for every N ≥ 1 at most C N^{G−γ} elements n ∈ [1, N]^G have Ξ(n) (a) not defined over Q or (b) isogenous to some B in H; the others can be taken Hodge generic, and for g = 2, 3, 5 any γ < 1 works.

items.name: Corollary 1.6: a rational fourfold isogenous to no Jacobian, if A_4 is unirational over Q
items.statement: If A_4 is unirational over Q, there is a principally polarized abelian fourfold defined over Q and Hodge generic that is not isogenous to any Jacobian.

items.name: Many isogeny classes among Ψ^{-1}(n)
items.statement: The Ψ^{-1}(n), n ∈ [1, N]^G, represent at least C_0^{-1}N^{G−ε} isogeny classes for every ε > 0, C_0 = C_0(Ψ, ε) > 0 (by the isogeny estimates [26] and the subgroup count, as at the end of §2).

items.name: Few CM points among the candidates
items.statement: The number of n ∈ [1, N]^G for which Ψ^{-1}(n) (or Ξ(n)) has CM is ≪ 1, via bounded field degree, the Pila–Tsimerman Galois lower bound [34, Conj. 7.1] (proved by Tsimerman [42] for g ≤ 6 unconditionally and for g ≥ 7 under GRH) and [34, Lemma 7.4].

items.name: Galois orbits of CM points are large (Tsimerman)
items.statement: The degree of the field of definition of a CM point of A_g grows as a positive power of the discriminant of its CM order (Pila–Tsimerman [34, Conj. 7.1], proved by Tsimerman [42], [44]).
items.note: Review: LD.6 builds its applications "from separate Galois-orbit bounds" and requires "independent orbit … suppliers", so it takes this bound as an input rather than planning it, and no other layer plans it. PAPER-TSIMERMAN-18, PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18 and PAPER-YUAN-ZHANG-18 route the CM Galois-orbit lower bounds, with the averaged Colmez formula their proof needs, to the accepted Part II "Complex multiplication and explicit reciprocity, Part II: CM heights and Galois-orbit bounds"; this item joins it (route 8). The paper cites [42] (g ≤ 6 unconditionally, all g under GRH) and [44].

items.name: Compact real-analytic interpolation image meeting algebraic isogeny classes
items.statement: For g≥2, choose distinct interpolation parameters t_n∈[1,2] and representatives τ_n of all algebraic moduli points, modified by Sp_{2g}(ℚ) within their isogeny classes. Newton interpolation constructs matrices F_x,F_w of entire functions, real on the real line, with F_x(t_n)=x_n and F_w(t_n)=w_n, such that F(t)=F_x(t)+i(I+F_w(t)F_w(t)^t) lies in H_g for real t∈[1,2]. Its compact real-analytic parametrized image K=J(F([1,2])) meets every isogeny class represented by A_g(ℚ̄). No embedded-curve or global closed analytic hypersurface assertion is part of this construction.
items.note: The Cholesky input is in Tau Ceti f790474: TauCeti.cholesky (LinearAlgebra/Matrix/Cholesky/Basic.lean), with TauCeti.continuous_cholesky and TauCeti.choleskyHomeomorph (Cholesky/Topology.lean). The construction uses only that the lower-triangular factor depends continuously on the matrix, not the Lipschitz form (50) (review). E13 records the failed global closed-hypersurface endpoint. The obstruction and a precisely gated local replacement specification are in /74. The entire matrix functions are not asserted to take every complex parameter into H_g; positivity is proved on the real interval, with local complex neighborhoods where appropriate.
proofOutline: Use continuity of the Cholesky factor on the positive-definite real symmetric matrices to choose w_n for each sufficiently close positive z_n. Use Sp_{2g}(ℚ)-density to select isogenous τ_n meeting each successive Newton-coefficient tolerance, as in pp.668–669.

Apply the existing Newton-series construction with coefficient bounds ensuring locally uniform convergence of the matrix entries; their values are real for real t. F_x is symmetric and I+F_wF_w^t is positive definite on [1,2]. Thus F stays in H_g there and K is compact by continuity of J. Interpolation at t_n proves the isogeny-class coverage.
Stop at the parametrized image. Local analytic dependence of coordinate functions is not a proof that equations on different chart domains extend or glue into a hypersurface in all A_g.

tests: For real w and nonzero v, vᵗ(I+wwᵗ)v=‖v‖²+‖wᵗv‖²>0, so the image stays in H_g.
Image compactness and real-analytic parametrization do not imply the image is a closed complex analytic hypersurface.
The interpolation parameters lie in the real interval; a complex continuation needs an explicitly smaller parameter neighborhood.

items.name: Igusa's modular form and the Schottky relation for g = 4
items.statement: F_g(τ) = 2^g U_g(τ) − V_g(τ)² with U_g = Σ θ_{mm*}(τ)^{16}, V_g = Σ θ_{mm*}(τ)^8 over m, m* ∈ 2^{-1}Z^g/Z^g is a Γ-form of weight 8; it vanishes identically on A_g for g ≤ 3, and for g = 4 its zero locus is the closure of the Jacobian locus (Grushevsky [16, Th. 3.8]).

items.name: Products lie in the closure of the Jacobian locus in genus 4
items.statement: For block-diagonal τ, U_g and V_g factor as products; hence F_4 vanishes on products of two principally polarized abelian surfaces and on products of an elliptic curve with a principally polarized abelian threefold, which therefore lie in the closure of the Jacobian locus of A_4.

items.name: Quotients of abelian varieties by finite subgroups
items.statement: For an abelian variety A over a field of characteristic 0 and a finite subgroup G ⊂ A, the quotient A/G is an abelian variety and A → A/G is an isogeny of degree #G. Every isogeny f : A → B identifies B with A/ker f, and deg f = #ker f.
items.locator: §1.1, p. 636 (A/G principally polarized when #G is a g-th power); end of §2, p. 644 ("E_j is isomorphic to E/G"); proof of Lemma 5.1(b), p. 658 ("isomorphic to A″/Γ")
items.note: Added in review. AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A3 plans "for a finite locally free subgroup, construct the fppf quotient abelian scheme and prove its universal property". Tau Ceti f790474 has isogenies of abelian varieties but no quotient or degree.

items.name: Degree and Rosati length of endomorphisms
items.statement: Let B be a principally polarized abelian variety of dimension n with Rosati length ℓ (item 15). (i) deg(v) = det ρ(v) is a homogeneous polynomial function of degree 2n on End(B), so deg(m_1v_1 + ··· + m_rv_r) = P(m_1, …, m_r) with P homogeneous of degree 2n. (ii) ℓ(uv) ≤ ℓ(u)ℓ(v) ([27, Lemma 2.2]). (iii) deg(v) ≤ ℓ(v)^{2n} ([27, Lemma 2.3]). For B = A × Ã, n = 2g, this gives (30) and (31).
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 4.2, (30) and (31), p. 656 ("It is well known that the degree …"; [27, Lemmas 2.2 and 2.3, p. 644])
items.note: Added in review. AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A2 plans Rosati involutions but not these trace-form inequalities, Tau Ceti f790474 has the endomorphism ring of an abelian variety but no degree function, and Mathlib has neither. (ii) is submultiplicativity of the norm defined by the positive Riemann form; (iii) is the inequality of arithmetic and geometric means on the eigenvalues of ρρ′.

items.name: Degree of a projective variety through generic linear projections
items.statement: Let V ⊂ P^r_C be an irreducible projective variety of dimension G < r. For generic linear forms χ_1, …, χ_{G+2}, the projection V ⇢ P^{G+1} is birational onto a hypersurface of degree deg V, so if the image lies in the zero set of a nonzero homogeneous polynomial of degree δ, then deg V ≤ δ. A generically finite projection V ⇢ P^G has degree at most deg V.
items.locator: §5.2, p. 666 ("the degree of the Zariski closure of the variety V_e … is at most 2D"; "This makes it clear that D_Ψ ≤ 2^{16g⁴−1}")
items.note: Added in review. It turns the relation P(χ_1², …, χ_{G+2}²) = 0, of degree 2D in the χ_i, into deg V̄_16 ≤ 2D, and bounds D_Ψ by that degree. No layer plans projective degree under projections; AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry R09.1–R09.2 plan Hilbert polynomials, whose leading coefficient gives the degree.

items.name: A field of definition of bounded degree over the field of moduli
items.statement: For a principally polarized abelian variety Ã over Q̄ with moduli point x ∈ A_g(Q̄) and field of moduli Q(x), there is a field of definition K̃ ⊇ Q(x) of Ã with [K̃ : Q(x)] ≤ c(g): lift x to the fine moduli space A_{g,3} of principally polarized abelian varieties with full level-3 structure and take the residue field of the lift.
items.locator: §5.1, p. 663 ("the number of different π_τ(ρ_σ) = τ̃_σ is ≫ D̃"), with (33) on p. 660; likewise p. 650 for g = 1
items.note: Added in review. (33) bounds m̃ by the degree D̃ of a field of definition, while the Pila count needs the number of Galois conjugates of the moduli point, which is the degree of the field of moduli; the paper passes between them without comment. PELModuli M2 and M5 own the Siegel moduli problem with level structure, which this imports.

items.name: Supplementary rational 16-torsion claim — unresolved arithmetic descent
items.statement: Unresolved supplementary target, not part of Theorem 1.1: construct the hypersurface-avoiding principally polarized A over a number field K of degree ≤2^{16g⁴} with every point of A[16] K-rational. The printed inference from Γ(16,32) to its theta coordinate field is insufficient. This conclusion is gated until the arithmetic fine-level comparison and its complete degree bound are proved.
items.locator: Published p.637, sentence after Theorem 1.1; closing paragraph of §5.2, p.666 (E14)

gate.required: A comparison of the theta Q-model with the arithmetic full-level moduli model/universal scheme, including polarization, all descent extensions, and the final degree bound.

proofOutline: Import arithmetic fine-level moduli and universal principally polarized abelian schemes from PELModuli M2/M5, torsion and perfect Galois-equivariant Weil pairing from AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A3, and analytic level comparison from A5. Do not reconstruct those theories here.

Separate the theta coordinate field K_θ, a field K_A carrying a polarized model, K_cyc=K_A(ζ_16), and a field K_tor carrying a full symplectic level basis. A perfect equivariant Weil pairing implies μ_16⊆K_tor: an exact-order-16 point pairs with some torsion point to a primitive root, fixed by Galois when both points are rational. Cyclotomic containment is necessary, not sufficient for splitting the entire representation.

For a proposed finite arithmetic comparison cover Y→V_16 over F_Y and map Ψ_Y=Ψ∘π, compute D(Y,Ψ_Y)=[F_Y:ℚ][F_{Ψ_Y}:ℚ]D_{Ψ_Y}, including the comparison-cover degree. If instead extending a residue field, track [K_tor:ℚ]=[K_tor:K_cyc][K_cyc:K_A][K_A:K_θ][K_θ:ℚ]. Bound [K_cyc:K_A]≤φ(16)=8 and prove every other factor. Do not automatically multiply both descriptions and double-count the same extension.

Only enable the supplementary target after proving the resulting total ≤2^{16g⁴} and the desired moduli interpretation. Neither that inequality nor sufficiency of adjoining ζ_16 is established here. The main theorem’s D remains unchanged.

tests: A real number field cannot contain all μ_16, hence cannot define full rational 16-torsion on a principally polarized A.
A coordinate field, a field of moduli, a field of definition and a torsion field are not interchangeable.
Adjoining ζ_16 alone is not an acceptance test for full rational torsion; demand a trivialized Galois module and the actual degree calculation.

items.name: Closed analytic hypersurface obstruction and gated local replacement
items.statement: For g≥2, every globally closed pure analytic hypersurface of A_g(ℂ) is algebraic: its closure in the projective Satake compactification is analytic by Remmert–Stein and algebraic by Chow. Consequently the §5.4 interpolation image cannot be promoted to a transcendental globally closed analytic hypersurface meeting every algebraic isogeny class. A local/germ or nonclosed replacement is a separate unresolved target, with its ambient domain specified before use.
items.locator: Masser–Zannier §5.4 pp.668–670 (E13); Le Fourn (2019) 6.4, p.181; Demailly Chapter II (8.7), p.118 and (8.10), p.121

gate.required: For a local replacement specify U⊆A_g(ℂ) open, K⊆U, and a pure codimension-one closed analytic W_U⊆U containing K, and prove the extension/compatibility of local equations there; alternatively specify and prove a germwise/nonclosed statement. No replacement is enabled by this packet.

proofOutline: Put G=g(g+1)/2. Import the projective Satake compactification from ShimuraCompactifications C5 and analytic subsets/Chow/Remmert–Stein suppliers from ComplexComparisonPartII C0/C4. Its boundary has dimension G−g; a pure hypersurface has local dimension G−1>G−g for g≥2.

Remmert–Stein applies to the singular ambient complex space as well: closure across that boundary is analytic. Embed the projective compactification in projective space and apply Chow. Restriction to A_g gives the original W because W was closed there. The main algebraic hypersurface-avoidance theorem then rules out coverage of every algebraic isogeny class by such W.

Local equations on overlapping neighborhoods cannot simply be multiplied without a common domain or compatible extensions. The source’s finite-cover/compactness argument does not provide that gluing. Keep /66 as the interpolation endpoint while the local replacement remains gated.
tests: For g=2, G−1=2 exceeds boundary dimension G−g=1; for g=1 equality prevents this argument, so the elliptic construction /40 is unchanged.
Relative closedness in an open neighborhood U is distinct from global closedness in A_g.
Finite many equations on different domains do not define a product on their union without extensions.

routes.title: Faltings finiteness, semisimplicity and isogeny theorems, Part II: Quantitative isogeny estimates
routes.brief: The same Part II that PAPER-TSIMERMAN-18 proposes under this id, for the Masser–Wüstholz factorization estimates; this paper adds the rest of the Masser–Wüstholz method to it. Final theorems: (1) the isogeny estimate (Masser–Wüstholz, Isogeny estimates for abelian varieties, and finiteness theorems, Ann. of Math. 137 (1993)): isogenous A, B over a number field of degree D admit an isogeny of degree bounded polynomially in D and h(A), exponents depending on g, with the elliptic case in the explicit form c D²(log D)²(1 + h(j))² of Gaudron–Rémond (Comment. Math. Helv. 89 (2014)); (2) the endomorphism estimate (Masser–Wüstholz, Math. Z. 215 (1994)): D(A) ≤ c max{D, h(A)}^λ for the discriminant of End(A) with respect to the Rosati form; (3) the lower bound for cusp forms at algebraic points (Masser–Wüstholz, Periods and minimal abelian subvarieties, Ann. of Math. 137 (1993), Lemmas 8.4 and 8.6). Cover the analytic and rational representations of endomorphisms, the Rosati length and discriminant, and the period theorem that drives (1) and (2). Import Faltings heights and their isogeny variation from ArakelovGeometryAndAbelianHeights (R35.3–R35.4), duals, quotients, Hom and the Rosati involution from AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli (A2, A3, A6), successive minima from GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic (GN.1), Weil heights and transcendence methods from DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence (DT.0, DT.3), and the qualitative isogeny theorems from FaltingsFinitenessAndIsogenyTheorems (R28).
routes.reason: FaltingsFinitenessAndIsogenyTheorems owns the qualitative isogeny theorem (R28.2) but no layer bounds isogeny degrees or endomorphism discriminants. PAPER-TSIMERMAN-18 already proposes this Part II for the effective isogeny bound, so the endomorphism and period estimates, which share its transcendence method and its inputs, belong in the same roadmap rather than in a second one; they are imports of the paper's own roadmap, not part of it. Review: the route coalesces exactly with PAPER-TSIMERMAN-18's accepted route 10 (same parent, id, title and area). RICHARD-YAFAEV-25's accepted route 1 sent "Masser–Wüstholz refinements of the Tate conjecture" to R28.4; the design should keep all Masser–Wüstholz estimates in this Part II. Item 70, the degree and Rosati-length inequalities behind Lemma 4.2, joins item 15 here.

routes.title: Abelian varieties isogenous to no Jacobian (Masser–Zannier)
routes.brief: Plan Masser–Zannier, Abelian varieties isogenous to no Jacobian (Ann. of Math. 191 (2020), 635–674). Final theorems exactly as the paper states them: Theorem 1.1 (for any hypersurface H of A_g, g ≥ 2, a Hodge generic A over a field of degree at most 2^{16g⁴}, isogenous to nothing in H; the supplementary torsion remark is isolated and gated in /73, not included in the main theorem), Corollary 1.2 (g ≥ 4: isogenous to no Jacobian), Theorem 1.3 (at most C N^{G−γ} of the n ∈ [1, N]^G fail, for γ < 1/2, any γ < 1 when g is odd or 2, 6; D(Ã, Ψ) = [F̃ : Q][F_Ψ : Q]D_Ψ; further, there exist Ã, Ψ defined over Q with D(Ã, Ψ) = 2^{16g⁴}), Corollary 1.4 (a euclidean-dense set of pairwise non-isogenous examples), Theorem 1.5 and Corollary 1.6 (conditional on unirationality, g ≤ 5), and Theorem 1.7 (elliptic curves E_{n1+in2} versus a real algebraic curve, at most C N(log N)^{10} exceptions). Cover: the Jacobian locus and its closure, Igusa's fundamental-domain estimates, the integer matrices of isogenies (Lemmas 2.1, 4.1, 4.2), heights of period matrices (Lemma 4.3), the counting lemmas 3.1–3.3 and 5.1–5.2, the Pila-blocks argument with the Hodge-generic versus weakly-special step, Siegel Λ-forms, Igusa's order bound, theta constants of level Γ(16, 32) and the degree bound 2^{16g⁴−1}, the isogeny-class and CM counts, the elliptic real-analytic curve and the compact higher-dimensional interpolation image meeting algebraic isogeny classes, with the global closed-hypersurface assertion rejected and any local replacement gated in /74, and the genus-4 Igusa form with products. Import: A_g from PELModuli (M2, M5); the Siegel datum and special points from ShimuraData (D4, D5), with the Mumford–Tate definition of Hodge genericity from D1; o-minimal counting and blocks from the early counting content of LogicAndDefinabilityInNumberTheory LD.6, and uniformization definability, Ax–Lindemann and weakly special geometry from the shared LogicAndDefinabilityPartII (route 9); the definition of Galois genericity from ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations (R01.6); Hilbert irreducibility with Cohen's count from InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups (IG.2); modular polynomials from ModularCurvesPartII (R13.4); heights from ArakelovGeometryAndAbelianHeights (R35.3–R35.4); the isogeny and endomorphism estimates from FaltingsFinitenessAndIsogenyTheoremsPartII; Jacobians from the Tau Ceti JacobianChallenge. Review (REV-PAPER-MASSER-ZANNIER-20): also cover the Galois-genericity inputs Serre's open image for End = Z in dimensions g odd, 2, 6, Deligne's open monodromy of the universal family and the implications of Cadoret and Pink (items 6, 24, 25), importing Faltings' semisimplicity and isogeny theorems from FaltingsFinitenessAndIsogenyTheorems (R28.4) and A_g with level structure from PELModuli (M2, M5); Deligne's absolute Hodge theorem, which Pink's implication uses, is planned nowhere and is a source-closure obligation. Import Siegel sets and fundamental sets from AdelicAlgebraicGroups (AA.3) and ShimuraVarieties (V0) for item 9, which adds only the Minkowski-reduced domain and Igusa's estimates; Siegel modular forms, their transformation law and Fourier expansions from AutomorphicBundles (B4, B5) and ShimuraVarieties (V2) for item 50, which adds only ord; the degree of a projective variety under projections (item 71) and the bounded field of definition over the field of moduli (item 72); and the CM Galois-orbit bound from the Part II "Complex multiplication and explicit reciprocity, Part II: CM heights and Galois-orbit bounds" (route 8). Binding verified fixes: E13 rules out a globally closed transcendental analytic hypersurface for g≥2; /66 ends at the compact real-analytic parametrized image. A local replacement must specify its open ambient U and relative closedness and prove chart compatibility before activation. E14 gates the supplementary rational 16-torsion assertion; import PELModuli M2/M5 and AbelianSchemes A3/A5 and prove the theta/fine-level arithmetic comparison. Account for cyclotomic and all further descent degrees using /73; neither adjoining ζ_16 alone nor the unchanged geometric degree is sufficient. The main Theorem 1.1, its field bound and algebraic hypersurface avoidance remain intact. Import Satake geometry from ShimuraCompactifications C5 and analytic-closure/Chow suppliers from ComplexComparisonPartII C0/C4 for /74. Implement the stated APIs/tests and retain both unresolved gates explicitly. Supplier requests attached to this extraction require the general singular-space Remmert–Stein extension at ComplexComparisonPartII C4 and the exact Siegel boundary-dimension specialization at ShimuraCompactifications C5; the current stage texts do not explicitly export those adapters. The owner designs must register and prove them before the /74 obstruction is implemented formally.

sourceIssues.reason: Permissibility needs Gm(n + in0, n − in0) ≢ 0 in n for every m ≤ M, as in the proof of Lemma 3.2. The sketch shows that the obstacle can occur only when ψ(m) ≤ d and, for one such m, excludes at most deg Gm ≤ 2dψ(m)² values of n0. For d ≥ 3 more than one m qualifies (m = 1, and m = 2 since ψ(2) = 3), and the excluded sets need not coincide: for d = 3 the union bound is 2·3·(1 + 9) = 60 > 54 = 2d³. The existence of some n0 bounded polynomially in d is unaffected; whether 2d³ + 1 itself holds is not settled here.
